[[File:Sinaceur.jpg|thumb|Hourya Benis Sinaceur]]
{{Short description|Moroccan philosopher}}
'''Hourya Sinaceur''' is a Moroccan philosopher.  She is an expert in the theory and history of mathematics.

==Biography==
Hourya Benis was born in 1940 in [[Casablanca]] in Morocco.<ref>"Hommage à Rabat à la philosophe marocaine Hourya Benis Sinaceur" in ''MAP'', 16 Nov. 2007 [http://www.vivrefemme.net/Hommage-a-Rabat-a-la-philosophe-marocaine-Hourya-Benis-Sinaceur_a985.html] retrieved 32-2-2009)</ref> Sinaceur worked for [[Paris-Sorbonne University]] and the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] which is also in Paris, and the URS{{What?|date=February 2022}} in [[Rabat]]. She has also served as a member of the National French Committee of History and Philosophy of Science (Comité National Francais d'Histoire et de Philosophie des Sciences.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www6.inra.fr/comitedhistoire/Media/fichiers/CNFHPS|title=Statuts / Composition / Actualités passées / Historique|publisher=Comité national français d’histoire et de philosophie des sciences|year=2011|accessdate=2020-06-15|archive-date=2021-07-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210714235159/https://www6.inrae.fr/comitedhistoire/content/download/3005/30160/version/1/file/cnfphs.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Books==
She is the author of the book ''Corps et Modèles'' (1991), translated into English as ''Field and Models: From Sturm to Tarski and Robinson'' (Birkhauser, 2003).<ref>Reviews of ''Field and Models'': Javier Echeverría (1992), ''Theoria'', {{JSTOR|23915307}}; Albert C. Lewis (1992), ''Isis'', {{JSTOR|233959}}; Peter M. Neumann (1992), ''British Journal for the History of Science'', {{JSTOR|4027271}}; Pascal Gribomont (1997), ''Revue Internationale de Philosophie'', {{JSTOR|23954471}}</ref> and of ''Functions and Generality of Logic: Reflections on Dedekind's and Frege's logicisms'' (Springer, 2015).<ref>Review of ''Functions and Generality of Logic'': Risto Vilkko, {{MR|3363186}}</ref>
